# DUM-E

> A local-first desktop app for Windows that turns coding-agent CLIs into a self-coordinating team of robots on a shared 2D lab floor. OpenCode is the default engine.

DUM-E is an Electron app (v0.1.1, MIT licensed) for Windows 10+ x64. Every agent runs a real CLI session in a real PTY — not a chat wrapper. Each agent gets its own working directory, long-term memory, an inbox/outbox, and access to a shared task board. DUM-E is the orchestrator robot: it spawns first, reads the board, delegates to workers, routes messages, supervises, and escalates to the human, who stays in control.

## Engines

- **OpenCode** — the default engine
- **Qwen Code** — supported
- **Claude Code** — supported
- **OpenAI Codex** — bridged
- **Custom endpoints** — configurable; local LLM endpoints supported

DUM-E coordinates the engines; it does not replace them. Bring your own keys where an engine requires them.

## What it does

- Real terminals — one live PTY per robot, rendered with xterm.js; open one, or pool every robot's terminal at once
- Long-term memory — one `memory.md` per robot, condensed as it grows, with optional semantic search
- Agent-to-agent mail — file-based outbox → inbox routing with reply tracking; hop caps stop two robots talking forever
- Task kanban — DUM-E creates, assigns, and moves the cards on one shared board (`tasks.json`)
- Orchestrated delegation — DUM-E spawns first, delegates work, routes messages, supervises, and escalates to you
- Cost guardrails — token caps, cost caps, a max-turns limit per robot, and a circuit breaker
- Triggers — scheduled missions, HTTP webhooks, and Slack ingestion
- Voice control — push-to-talk dictation into any robot, and voice orchestration for the floor (bring your own key)
- Shareable hires — a robot's whole setup travels as a `dum-e://hire` deep link a teammate can spawn as-is
- Procedural art — every robot portrait is drawn in code in the repo; no third-party product art

## Local-first

No telemetry. No analytics. No DUM-E cloud. Your data stays on your machine; engine providers may have their own policies. Builds are unsigned — Windows SmartScreen may ask you to trust the app on first launch.

## Requirements

- Windows 10+ x64 (primary target)
- Internet connection on first use
- One engine CLI installed and logged in
- DUM-E installs Node.js and any missing agent CLIs itself on first use; you only need Node when building from source
- Linux: AppImage build configuration exists, but no Linux release asset is published yet
- macOS: build configuration exists, experimental
